why_angle: The cited rivals list the C300 DC's port ratings but never explain the cable rule: 100 W over USB-C is only 20 V × 5 A, so it needs a 5 A e-marked cable, and an ordinary 3 A cable stops at 60 W. They also never say which boxes include such a cable. The Jackery 300D's handle is a 140 W USB-C cable (Jackery store), Anker lists a USB-C cable in the C300 DC box, and the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 ships with AC and car cables only. This corrects angles C and D, which said the 300D ships without a USB-C cable.

page.desc: Jackery Explorer 300D vs Anker SOLIX C300 DC, BLUETTI Elite 30 V2, Jackery Explorer 300 and EcoFlow RIVER 3: weight, capacity, 100 W USB-C ports, the cable each needs for 100 W, and laptop charges per weekend.
page.answer: Short answer. The small power station under 10 lb that charges a laptop at 100 W USB-C for a weekend is the Jackery Explorer 300D: 5.5 lb weight, 288 Wh capacity, two 140 W USB-C ports and a 140 W USB-C cable in the box. A plain 3 A cable caps 100 W USB-C at 60 W.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • A weekend of laptop work uses less than half of a 288 Wh station. The Gadgeteer kept an M1 MacBook Pro plugged into the Anker C300 DC through normal use, and the station dropped from 70% to 7% over three days. (70% − 7%) × 288 Wh ÷ 3 days ≈ 60 Wh a day, so two days ≈ 121 Wh, or 42% of 288 Wh.
  • Laptop charges per unit. techtest.org got 269.65 Wh out of the Anker C300X DC (the EU DC-only sister of the C300 DC) at USB-C 20 V/5 A, which is the 100 W condition. 269.65 Wh ÷ a 60 Wh laptop battery ≈ 4.5 full charges, before the laptop's own charging losses.
  • A steady 100 W drains a station much faster. The Technology Man measured 244 Wh from the Elite 30 V2's DC outputs. 244 Wh ÷ 100 W ≈ 2.4 hours at full draw. 100 W is the fastest a laptop can charge, not how much energy it uses over a whole day.
  • Battery per pound. 288 Wh ÷ 5.5 lb = 52 Wh/lb for the 300D. 288 ÷ 9.5 lb = 30 Wh/lb for the Elite 30 V2. 245 ÷ 7.7 lb = 32 Wh/lb for the RIVER 3.
  • Topping up in the car. The 300D's car input is 96 W max (Jackery). 121 Wh ÷ 96 W ≈ 1.3 hours of driving puts back a weekend of laptop use.

Why the cable decides whether the laptop gets 100 W

A USB-C port gives 100 W only as 20 V × 5 A. USB-IF requires every certified USB-C to USB-C cable to be labelled either 60 W or 240 W, and a cable that carries 20 V at 3 A gets the 60 W logo. 20 V × 3 A = 60 W, so with that cable the laptop charges at 60 W whatever the station's port is rated for. Texas Instruments notes that any cable rated above 3 A must carry an electronic marker chip. Look for a cable labelled 100 W (5 A) or 240 W.

  • Jackery Explorer 300D: Jackery's store says the handle is a built-in 2-in-1 USB-C strap that delivers 140 W. Plug the laptop into Type-C1 or C2 (140 W max, with 20 V × 5 A and 28 V × 5 A profiles). Type-C3 tops out at 65 W (20 V × 3.25 A) and can't reach 100 W with any cable.
  • Anker SOLIX C300 DC: Anker lists a USB-C to C cable in the box, and The Gadgeteer reports it as a 140 W cable. In Anker's sharing table as The Gadgeteer reproduces it, the 100 W port drops to 30 W once all three USB-C ports are in use, and with all five outputs in use the two 140 W ports fall to 60 W each. Anker's US store showed it as sold out on 2026-11-14.
  • BLUETTI Elite 30 V2: BLUETTI's box list is the unit, an AC charging cable, a car charging cable, a grounding screw and the manual. There is no USB-C cable, so add a 5 A cable such as {buy:baseus-usb-c-cable-100w}. The Technology Man measured the battery dropping to 24% in 20 hours with the DC outputs on, about 11 W of parasitic drain. Switch DC off between charges, or turn Eco mode on, so the battery isn't emptied before Sunday. With that habit it is the under-10 lb pick if you also need a wall outlet: {buy:bluetti-elite-30-v2}.
  • EcoFlow RIVER 3: ChargerLAB's teardown lists its one USB-C port at 100 W max, reached only at 20 V × 5 A, so it needs a 5 A cable too.
  • EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC: The Solar Lab lists it at 6 lb with two 140 W USB-C ports, and measured about 2 Wh used over 24 hours while switched on with nothing connected. Its review unit came without a charging cable.

Not recommended

Jackery Explorer 300 v2. Jackery's US store says it is sold out and points shoppers to the new Explorer 300. It weighs 8.1 lb and has one 100 W USB-C port. The Explorer 300D stores the same 288 Wh at 2.6 lb less (8.1 − 5.5) with two 140 W ports. If you want an AC outlet, the new Explorer 300 (7.5 lb, 292 Wh) replaces it.
